# Five Ways Governors Can Deliver Tech Wins in the First 100 Days


November 23, 2026


by Olivia Owens


##


A new governor’s first 100 days are an opportunity to establish priorities, build momentum, and demonstrate progress. As incoming administrations assemble leadership teams and shape legislative and budget agendas, technology can help turn those priorities into visible results.


Meaningful progress doesn’t always require major investments or entirely new systems. States already have technology platforms, vendor relationships, and digital infrastructure that can help new administrations move faster. The opportunity is to understand what’s in place, identify where it can do more, and focus on improvements that make a difference for residents and state employees.


"New administrations come into office with ambitious priorities and a critical first 100 days to demonstrate progress. Some of the most meaningful early wins come from building on what’s already working, strengthening collaboration across agencies, and identifying practical opportunities to improve government services for residents," says Sandi Miller, Policy & Advocacy Director at Tyler Technologies.


For transition teams, the challenge is knowing where to focus. These five strategies can help governors turn early priorities into measurable results.


## 1. Make the Governor’s Website an Early Priority


A new administration’s website is one of its first opportunities to communicate priorities and connect with residents. Updating the governor’s digital presence can establish the administration’s identity, share its agenda, and make important information easier to find.


In the first 100 days, transition teams should evaluate the existing website, update leadership and policy information, improve navigation, and create a central source for announcements, executive orders, and resident resources.


When a state already has a website platform and support contract in place, these improvements may be possible without launching a new technology initiative. Tyler can help administrations build on existing digital platforms to deliver an accessible, engaging online experience from day one.


## 2. Make Government Easier to Navigate With AI


Residents shouldn’t need to understand government structure to find answers or access services. A Resident AI Assistant gives people a conversational way to get information, navigate services, and find answers around the clock. It can also reduce repetitive inquiries and free state employees to focus on more complex work.


States are already demonstrating the impact. Indiana’s Ask Indiana has answered more than 260,000 questions, attracted more than 87,000 users in its first month, and supports more than 60 languages. In Nebraska, an AI assistant has handled 136,000 inquiries without staff intervention, with 19% occurring outside normal business hours. The state has also seen driver and license-related call volume decrease by up to 20%.


These results show how one strategic investment can improve access, expand language accessibility, and reduce the burden on state employees.


As Elliot Flautt, Director of State AI and Data Solutions at Tyler, explains:


## New administrations don’t have to launch major technology initiatives to make a meaningful impact. Sometimes, one strategic investment can put a state on an entirely new trajectory. Whether it’s using AI to make government services more accessible or automating time-consuming processes, the key is identifying opportunities to deliver measurable results quickly while building momentum for longer-term modernization.


Elliot Flautt


Director of State AI and Data Solutions
Tyler Technologies


## 3. Reduce Administrative Burdens Through Document Automation


Some of the most meaningful efficiency gains happen behind the scenes. Manual, document-heavy processes can slow employees, create backlogs, and make it harder for agencies to deliver timely services.


Document Automation can streamline repetitive work, extract and validate information, and improve processing accuracy without requiring agencies to replace entire systems.


Incoming administrations should ask agency leaders to identify high-volume processes that consume significant staff time or require repeated manual review. Nebraska, for example, is using Document Automation to support vehicle identification number (VIN) validation and logging. The initiative is expected to provide 100% audit capability across nearly 500,000 VIN records.


Targeted automation can help new administrations improve efficiency, strengthen oversight, and make better use of existing resources.


##### Put Your State’s Technology Investments to Work


As transition teams set priorities, Tyler can be a resource for evaluating existing capabilities, identifying opportunities, and connecting technology decisions to better government outcomes. Explore how[states can deliver early progress](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/resource-downloads/how-state-cios-deliver-early-wins-with-existing-platforms) by building on existing platforms.


## 4. Get More From Technology and Contracts Already in Place


New governors inherit more than policy priorities and budget commitments. They also inherit technology platforms, vendor relationships, and existing service agreements that may offer opportunities for immediate progress.


During the first 100 days, transition teams should work with state CIOs and agency leaders to review existing technology investments and identify underused capabilities, opportunities to expand services, or improvements that can be made within current contracts.


Existing platforms and transaction-funded solutions may offer ways to introduce new capabilities without a large upfront investment or lengthy procurement process. Tyler can help administrations evaluate their technology landscape, understand available options, and identify practical opportunities to build on what they already have.


## 5. Set Priorities and Measure Early Results


The first 100 days aren’t enough time to solve every technology challenge, but they are enough time to establish direction and demonstrate progress.


Governors should work with CIOs and agency leaders to identify a focused set of technology priorities tied to administration goals. These might include improving access to services, reducing processing times, increasing employee productivity, or lowering the cost of government operations.


For each priority, establish measurable outcomes and identify what can realistically be accomplished within the first 100 days. Some states are also exploring public-facing dashboards to share progress on administration priorities, giving residents greater visibility into initiatives underway and how campaign commitments are translating into action. Quick improvements to existing platforms can demonstrate immediate value while longer-term initiatives take shape.


## Turn Early Progress Into Long-Term Momentum


From refreshing the governor’s website to expanding access through AI, automating manual processes, and getting more from existing technology investments, opportunities for meaningful progress are available from the start.


The key is knowing where to look and having the right partner to help turn those opportunities into action. Tyler Technologies works alongside state governments to help incoming administrations evaluate existing capabilities, identify achievable improvements, and connect their priorities to solutions that deliver measurable results.


The first 100 days can set the tone for an administration. With the right strategy and support, they can also establish momentum that carries well beyond the transition.
